translations.source_sense_description: een stuk metaal omvormen tot een munt

glosses: metallene Zahlungsmittel (Münzen) herstellen/prägen

examples.text: In der Münze münzte man Gold zu Goldmünzen.

glosses: etwas, was man sagt oder tut, ganz genau auf bestimmte Inhalte oder bestimmte Personen beziehen

examples.text: Die kaum verhohlenen Anschuldigungen waren eindeutig auf die Oppositionsführerin gemünzt.
„Diese Zusammenhänge hatte N weder durchdacht, noch erkannt, wie so vieles andere, was er ausschließlich zur Erfüllung ganz persönlicher Wünsche und alles zu seinem Vorteil gemünzt, unternahm.“

glosses: so umsetzen, dass man einen Vorteil praktisch nutzt

examples.text: „Der Feind mochte mit der Kampfkraft seiner Truppen überlegen sein, konnte dies zu Beginn der Schlacht jedoch in keinen Vorteil münzen.“

translations.source_sense_description: een stuk metaal omvormen tot een munt

glosses: A piece of currency, usually metallic and in the shape of a disc, but sometimes polygonal, or with a hole in the middle.

examples.text: ...the coins were of all countries and sizes - doubloons, and louis d'ors, and guineas, and pieces of eight...

glosses: A token used in a special establishment like a casino.
That which serves for payment or recompense.

examples.text: The loss of every present advantage to flesh and blood is repaid in a nobler coin.

glosses: Something in broad circulation or use.

examples.text:
Tho’ truths in manhood darkly join,
⁠Deep-seated in our mystic frame,
⁠We yield all blessing to the name
Of Him that made them current coin; […]

glosses: Money in general, not limited to coins.

examples.text: She spent some serious coin on that car!
It was the biggest thing in the town, and everybody I met was full of it. They were going to run an over-sea empire, and make no end of coin by trade.
Boy toy named Troy, used to live in Detroit, big dope dealer money he was getting some coin.

Of course, she [Charlie XCX] has a penchant for designer frames that cost upwards of $400. If you want to splurge on one of those exact pairs, go off. If you want to save some coin, I found similar options at more affordable brands and even some Amazon dupes. You’re welcome.

glosses: One of the suits of minor arcana in tarot, or a card of that suit.
A corner or external angle.
A small circular slice of food.

examples.text: For munchies try deep-fried jalapeño coins, jumbo Buffalo wings, and hush puppies with a sweet edge.
Spread out four bread and butter pickle coins on top, and sprinkle with onion.

glosses: Ellipsis of cryptocoin; a cryptocurrency.

examples.text: What's the best coin to buy right now?

glosses: To make of a definite fineness, and convert into coins, as a mass of metal.

examples.text: to coin silver dollars
to coin a medal

Many persons believe that the so-called "dollar of the daddies," weighing 412½ grains (nine tenths fine), having a ratio to gold of "16 to 1" in value when first coined, was the original dollar of the Constitution.

glosses: To make or fabricate (especially a word or phrase).

examples.text: Over the last century the advance in science has led to many new words being coined.
Not fearing outward force: So ſhall my Lungs / Coine words till their decay, againſt thoſe Meazels
Some tale, some new pretense, he daily coined, / To soothe his sister and delude her mind.

As a result, men turn to the women in their lives to fulfill their emotional needs. Ferrara and her coauthor are not the first to suggest that women bear the burden of mankeeping (although they did coin the term).

According to Collins Dictionary and Wiktionary, the term was coined in 2017 by journalist Anzer Ayoob, the term Chenabi is derived from the Chenab River, with the suffix “-i”, commonly used to denote belonging.

glosses: To acquire rapidly, as money; to make.

examples.text: [...] Tenants cannot coin their Rent juſt at Quarter-day, but muſt gather it up by degrees, and lodge it with them till Pay-day, or borrow it of thoſe who have it lying by them, [...]

translations.source_sense_description: een stuk metaal omvormen tot een munt

glosses: Transformer en monnaie, en argent comptant.

examples.text: Monétiser un métal.

glosses: Réduire à la seule valeur monétaire.

examples.text: Aujourd’hui, l’on a tout monétisé : ainsi l’on ne dit pas : « Monsieur un tel a été nommé procureur général, il va soutenir les intérêts de sa province, comme la Chalotais. » Non, erreur : « Monsieur un tel vient d’avoir une belle place ! procureur-général […] cela rapporte vingt mille francs de traitement.

glosses: Transformer en source de gain financier.

examples.text: Tout se passe comme si le rêve des blogueurs, après celui des libertaires de la radio, avait préparé le terrain aux spéculateurs, habiles à « monétiser » les illusions et les bonnes volontés.
Ça ne me fait pas rêver qu’une foule d’entrepreneurs désirent monétiser la connaissance de mes pas ou de mes fréquentations !
